question: During a study on the immune system, an investigator isolates and labels T cells from the cortex of the thymus. The T cells that do not bind cortical epithelial cells expressing MHC molecules undergo apoptosis within 3–4 days. Which of the following best describes the T cells during this phase of differentiation?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "T cells in the thymus" -> "undergo positive selection" -> "bind to MHC molecules" -> "T cells that do not bind undergo apoptosis" -> "CD4+ and CD8+ T cells are present" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Thymic cortex contains cortical epithelial cells" -> "cortical epithelial cells express MHC molecules" -> "T cells interact with MHC molecules" -> "T cells that do not bind undergo apoptosis" -> "CD4+ and CD8+ T cells are being differentiated" -> 90%

CHAIN: "T cell precursors migrate to the thymus" -> "T cell precursors undergo differentiation" -> "interaction with MHC molecules is crucial" -> "T cells that do not bind undergo apoptosis" -> "CD4+ and CD8+ T cells are the result" -> 80%

CHAIN: "T cells in the thymus" -> "undergo selection processes" -> "positive selection involves binding to MHC" -> "non-binding T cells undergo apoptosis" -> "CD4+ and CD8+ T cells are produced" -> 90%

CHAIN: "T cell precursors enter the thymus" -> "differentiate into T cells" -> "positive selection occurs in the cortex" -> "T cells that do not bind MHC undergo apoptosis" -> "CD4+ and CD8+ T cells are formed" -> 85%
analysis: During the differentiation of T cells in the thymus, those that do not successfully bind to MHC molecules presented by cortical epithelial cells undergo apoptosis. This process is part of positive selection, which primarily involves CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. The T cells that are being described in the question are in the early stages of differentiation and have not yet committed to a specific lineage (CD4+ or CD8+). Therefore, they are best described as CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, as they express both markers before selection occurs.
